info.description:
# napari-bboxes

Axis-aligned 2-D and 3-D bounding boxes (detections, annotations) as [napari](https://napari.org) layers that you can see **in every 2-D plane and in 3-D**, aligned with the image they belong to. napari's own layers cannot do this for 3-D boxes: a Shapes rectangle lives in one plane, and a Surface mesh shows nothing in 2-D slices (only faces lying entirely in the slice are drawn). napari-bboxes draws a 3-D box as a one-voxel **outline** on the image grid, computed on demand: an axial, coronal or sagittal slice shows the rectangle where it cuts the box, and the 3-D view shows only the box **edges**, so the content inside stays visible. The array costs no memory. ```bash pip install napari-bboxes ``` ## Usage ```python import napari from napari_bboxes import add_bboxes viewer = napari.Viewer() image = viewer.add_image(ct, affine=ct_affine) add_bboxes( viewer, mins=[[40, 60, 70], [10, 20, 30]], # inclusive corners in index coordinates of the image grid maxs=[[60, 90, 110], [18, 35, 44]], labels=[1, 2], # class per box scores=[0.97, 0.41], # optional names={1: "tumor", 2: "node"}, # optional display names colors={1: (230, 60, 60)}, # optional; other classes get palette colours grid_shape=ct.shape, affine=image.affine.affine_matrix, # same index -> world transform as the image: boxes align with it ) napari.run() ``` - **3-D boxes** become a Labels layer: each box has its own number, coloured by class, and hovering shows `name (label) score`. With labels or scores, a second layer shows that text on screen: in 2-D above the top-left corner of every box the current slice cuts (it follows the slice, the plane and 2-D/3-D switches), in 3-D at a box corner. `text=False` turns it off. - **2-D boxes** become a Shapes layer of rectangles, with the same text next to each box. - `bbox_layers(...)` returns the same as layer data tuples `(data, kwargs, layer_type)`, for napari readers. - `BoxShells(shape, bounds, mode)` is the lazy outline array on its own. `mode="auto"` (default) draws the box surface for 2-D slices and the edges for the 3-D view; `"faces"` or `"edges"` force one of them. Coordinates are array indices of a grid (voxel centres, inclusive bounds). Boxes in world or physical coordinates are converted by the caller: map the corners through the inverse of the image affine and take the bounding box. Used by [napari-mlarray](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/napari-mlarray) for the boxes stored in MLArray files. ## Development ```bash pip install -e ".[test]" pytest ``` ## License MIT
